title: ENERGY STAR Certified Residential Refrigerators
publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, ENERGY STAR
notes: Dataset p5st-her9; metadata at https://data.energystar.gov/api/views/p5st-her9.json returned name 'ENERGY STAR Certified Residential Refrigerators'. Model rows are recorded in energystar_refrigerators.csv (task 2.2): 1,793 rows from the 2026-09-26 Socrata pull (fields brand_name, model_number, annual_energy_use_kwh_yr), kept only for the retail brands GE, GE Profile, GE Adora, Cafe (also Café), Hotpoint, Whirlpool, Maytag, Amana, Frigidaire, Frigidaire Gallery, Samsung, LG, Kenmore, KitchenAid, Hisense, Insignia, Haier, Midea, Magic Chef, Danby, Galanz, Crosley, Bosch, Electrolux, Avanti, Summit, Arctic King, Comfee, Mainstays. A trailing '*' in the dataset means 'any of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, version code or blank'; model_normalized drops it, so only the base model (the blank case) matches exactly. A brand and model with more than one distinct annual kWh in the dataset (105 of them) is left out rather than picked between.

title: Study of Life Expectancy of Home Components, Table 1: Life Expectancy of Different Products/Items/Materials in the Home
publisher: National Association of Home Builders / Bank of America Home Equity
notes: February 2007 study; the URL is a third-party copy of the PDF, which was read in full text for this row. Table 1, '1. APPLIANCES': 'Refrigerators, Standard 13', 'Refrigerators, Compact 9', 'Freezers 11' (life in years), with the note 'Life expectancy is based on first-owner use.' Table source line: 'Appliance Magazine, Sep 2005 issue, Grainger'. Findings text: 'appliances are often replaced long before they are worn out because changes in styling, technology and consumer preferences make newer products more desirable.' A single point estimate, not a range: refrigerator.json uses 13 for both ends. ENERGY STAR's savings calculations assume a 12-year lifetime ('about $150 over the 12-year lifetime of the product', https://www.energystar.gov/products/refrigerators).

title: How does Afterpay work? (Pay in 4)
notes: Quoted from the page: 'We split the total order amount into 4 instalments, taken automatically every 2 weeks.' 'The customer pays the first instalment at the time of purchase.' 'When paying in four installments, there is always 0% interest and never additional fees when they pay on time.'
